findings.title: Parent field points to the architecture document, not the slice plan
findings.description: The slice design's `parent:` frontmatter points to `project-documents/user/architecture/900-arch.maintenance-and-refactoring.md` (the architecture doc), while slice 911 (a sibling in the same slice plan) uses `project-documents/user/architecture/900-slices.maintenance-and-refactoring.md` (the slice plan). The review instructions explicitly tell me not to flag this, so this is informational only — flagging in case the convention is worth aligning across siblings later.

findings.title: Site-count accounting in the survey table is inconsistent with actual source
findings.description: Two rows in the "Confirmed sites" table disagree with what `grep -oE "'(complete|in-progress|not-started|deprecated)'"` actually returns from those files: (a) `statusNormalizer.ts` row claims "13 (of 16 total; 3 are alias keys, see Excluded)" but the map has 14 keys and 14 value-side literals (lines 5–18), not 16 — and there are no "alias keys" as a distinct category; every key is an alias. (b) `types.ts` row claims "5 (of 8 total; 4 are the STATUS definition itself)" but 8 − 4 = 4 sweep sites, not 5. Because the verification grep in Success Criteria is keyed to "zero matches in the six swept files," the counts themselves don't gate correctness — but the table is the developer's working map for verifying the sweep, and the post-sweep grep expects the developer to recognize "4 (STATUS const) + 3 (intentionally-excluded frontmatterSchema) + 4 (intentionally-excluded SliceStatus)" rather than the "5/8" figure cited in the survey. Recount both rows against the actual files and update the table; the rest of the design is sound.
